item_name: RADIO COMMUNICATION, AIRMANSHIP, EMERGENCY PROCEDURES, GENERAL KNOWLEDGE.

observations.text: SP performed the R/T at the standard desired for this Training Section, establishing two-way communication with the ground station only after the IP had selected the frequency and passed the initial call. Clearance read-backs were made with the IP's wording. Marginal performance for the Section - independent use of the R/T, without the IP executing part of the communication, is expected to develop on the next sorties.

SP established two-way communication with the ground station and the other A/C using standard phraseology after the IP's verbal prompts, without the IP executing any part of the communication. Departure and approach clearances were read back correctly, although responses to calls were made with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP operated the R/T without the IP's intervention, with minor errors of phraseology in the initial contact after the frequency change, which were recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Instructions from the ground station were followed precisely and without misinterpretation throughout the instrument profile. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP was cognizant of the radio procedures and executed them without any support from the IP, obtaining contact with each station according to the standard procedures and phraseology. Radio communication was continuously monitored, calls were answered as soon as possible and no transmission interrupted communication in progress between the ground station and other A/C. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP operated the R/T with exceptional accuracy throughout the mission, from engine start up to engine shut down, using standard phraseology on every frequency without a single repeat request. Approach and GCA instructions were read back and executed precisely, with negligible deviations in wording, and initial contact after each frequency change was made without interrupting communication in progress. Radio management remained above the desired levels while cockpit workload was concentrated in the approach phase. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient familiarity with the operation of the radio control panel, did not select the assigned approach frequency and did not establish two-way communication with the ground station, with the result that the IP selected the frequency and executed the initial contact. The approach clearance was received and interpreted by the IP. Further study of the proper operation and use of the R/T is required.

SP communicated through the R/T at the standard desired for this Training Section, obtaining contact with the approach controller and reading back the clearance after the IP's verbal prompts. Non-standard wording in two position reports was recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Section - self-initiated use of the standard phraseology is expected to improve.

SP monitored radio communication continuously and responded to calls from the ground station without the IP's prompting, with minor errors in the phraseology of the holding report that were corrected in a timely manner. Instructions from the controller were followed without misinterpretation during the penetration and the approach. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the radio procedures without any support from the IP, obtaining contact with each station according to the standard procedures and phraseology and reading back all clearances accurately and rapidly. No transmission was made over communication in progress between the ground station and other A/C after the frequency changes. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP operated the R/T with exceptional precision throughout the instrument sortie, executing initial contact on every assigned frequency without prompting and without interrupting communication in progress. Read-backs of the departure clearance, of the holding instruction and of the successive approach clearances were complete and free of non-standard wording. Response to calls was immediate even while the A/C was being configured, demonstrating radio discipline above the desired levels. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized frequency management sequence, did not execute initial contact with the approach controller after the frequency change and did not read back the assigned altitude, with the result that the IP had to pass the call and clarify the clearance. Two calls addressed to the A/C remained unanswered. Further study of the standard R/T procedures and phraseology is required.

SP, due to non-standard phraseology that left the intention ambiguous to the controller, did not obtain contact with the ground station following the standard procedure and did not confirm the actual clearance in the read-back, with the result that the exchange was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts. The misinterpretation of the assigned approach was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP communicated through the R/T within the desired standards, monitoring the frequency continuously and responding to calls without the IP's intervention. On two occasions the position report was transmitted with non-standard wording and was self-corrected. Marginal performance for the Section - consistency in standard phraseology during the approach phase is expected to improve.

SP was cognizant of the radio procedures and executed them without any support from the IP, establishing two-way communication with the ground station and the other A/C accurately and rapidly. Every instruction was followed precisely and without misinterpretation, and initial contact after each frequency change was executed without interrupting communication in progress. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional operation and use of the R/T from engine start up to engine shut down, with standard phraseology on all frequencies and no request for a repeat by any station. Clearances for the departure, the holding and the successive approaches were read back completely and executed precisely, with negligible deviations in wording. Frequency management remained ahead of the A/C throughout the profile, above the desired levels for the Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized scan of the radio control panel during the descent, did not establish two-way communication with the arrival controller on the assigned frequency, with the result that the IP selected the correct frequency and executed the initial contact. The descent clearance was received and interpreted by the IP. Review of the proper operation and use of the R/T is required.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in stating "unable" when the clearance could not be complied with, did not request a repeat of the instruction that was not understood and did not confirm the assigned holding fix, with the result that the correct read-back was transmitted only after the IP's verbal prompts. The misinterpretation of the ground station instruction was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to a delayed transfer of attention to the radio control panel after the frequency change, executed initial contact late and transmitted the position report with non-standard wording, with the result of minor deviations from the standard phraseology, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Communication in progress between the ground station and other A/C was not interrupted.

SP executed the radio procedures within the desired standards, obtaining contact with each station without the IP's support and following all instructions without misinterpretation. Response to two calls during the approach phase was slower than the standard required for this Section, although the accuracy of the read-backs was maintained. Marginal performance for the Section - speed of response under approach workload is expected to improve.

SP demonstrated exceptional radio discipline throughout the instrument mission, executing every initial contact and every read-back with standard phraseology and without a single repeat request from any station. Instructions from the departure, the radar and the tower controllers were followed precisely and anticipated in the cockpit setup, with negligible deviations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated airmanship at the standard desired for this Training Section, maintaining orientation only while the IP identified the position of the A/C relative to the approach fix. Task prioritization during the penetration was set by the IP, who executed part of the cockpit management. Marginal performance for the Section - carrying out the required duties with reduced IP supervision is expected to develop on the next sorties.

SP maintained orientation during flight and monitored the Control and Performance Instruments after the IP's verbal prompts, without the IP taking over any part of the task management. The fuel state and the remaining flight time were assessed and the profile was adjusted accordingly, although contingencies were identified with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP prioritized the cockpit tasks without the IP's intervention, with minor lapses in the crosscheck of the A/C position against the Control and Performance Instruments that were recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Operational checks were performed according to the Check List and the SOPs and the alternate airfield option remained available throughout the profile. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated accurate awareness and judgment throughout the mission, maintaining orientation, crosschecking the A/C position against the Control and Performance Instruments and performing all operational checks according to the Check List, the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the SOPs. Tasks were placed in order without any item being dropped, decisions were clearly stated with their rationale and all duties were carried out with minimum IP supervision. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional airmanship for the level of the Training Section, correlating the ground situation, the A/C state and the traffic in the approach sequence, and adjusting the profile to the remaining fuel and the assigned holding time. Risk was assessed before each decision, contingencies and alternatives were accurately identified and the divert criteria for the alternate airfield were stated in advance. Task loading never approached saturation and no element of channelized attention appeared during the approaches. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a task sequence that concentrated the cockpit setup inside the procedure turn, did not maintain orientation relative to the approach fix and did not crosscheck the A/C position against the Control and Performance Instruments, with the result that the IP directed the correction and executed part of the navigation management. Contingencies for the missed approach were not identified. Further study of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the SOPs is required.

SP demonstrated airmanship at the standard desired for this Training Section, maintaining orientation and performing the operational checks after the IP's verbal prompts. The fuel state and the remaining flight time were reassessed with delay during the holding. Marginal performance for the Section - self-initiated task prioritization and monitoring of the A/C state are expected to improve.

SP managed the cockpit workload without the IP's intervention, with minor omissions in the operational checks that were recognized and corrected in a timely manner before the descent. Orientation was maintained throughout the profile and the decision to continue to the primary airfield was clearly stated with its rationale. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP correlated the A/C state, the weather and the traffic situation accurately and adjusted the execution of the mission to the remaining fuel and the assigned flight time. All operational checks were performed according to the Check List and the SOPs, tasks were placed in order without any item being dropped and all duties were carried out with minimum IP supervision. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional awareness and judgment throughout the instrument sortie, minimizing the effect of the adverse factors encountered and capitalizing on the sequence offered by the radar controller. Alternatives were identified before they were needed, every decision was clearly stated with its rationale and the workload was distributed so that no phase of the mission approached saturation. Orientation and the crosscheck of the A/C position against the Control and Performance Instruments were maintained with negligible deviations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized allocation of attention between the navigation setup and the control of the A/C, did not monitor the Control and Performance Instruments during the arc and did not maintain orientation relative to the arrival fix, with the result that the IP directed the recovery of the profile and executed part of the avionics management. The fuel required for the alternate airfield was not computed. Further study of the Local Area Procedures and the SOPs is required.

SP, due to workload management that left the approach checklist unfinished before the descent, did not put the cockpit tasks in order and did not identify the contingencies for the missed approach, with the result that the profile was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts. The saturation was recognized and relieved with delay, without an alternative course of action being selected in time.

SP demonstrated airmanship within the desired standards, maintaining orientation, performing the operational checks according to the Check List and carrying out the duties without the IP's intervention. On two occasions the crosscheck of the fuel state against the remaining flight time was made late and was self-corrected. Marginal performance for the Section - consistency in fuel and time management during the working phase is expected to improve.

SP demonstrated accurate awareness and judgment, correlating the A/C state with the clearance received and adjusting the profile to the available flight time and the assigned area. Risk was assessed before each decision, decisions were clearly stated with their rationale and flight discipline was maintained in the proper order of every procedure, with minimum IP supervision. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional airmanship, anticipating the effect of the reported weather on the approach minima and preparing the alternate airfield option before the descent was commenced. The multitask sequence was handled without any item being dropped, no element of channelized attention appeared and the capacity limits were never approached. Monitoring of the Control and Performance Instruments and their crosscheck with the A/C position remained precise, with negligible deviations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect order of priorities during the transition to the final approach segment, did not monitor the Control and Performance Instruments and did not maintain orientation relative to the runway, with the result that the IP directed the correction and executed part of the approach management. The requirement to break off the approach was not recognized. Review of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the SOPs is required.

SP, due to complacency in a familiar pattern that replaced an active scan, did not perform the operational checks in the proper order and did not reassess the fuel state against the remaining flight time, with the result that the profile was restored only after the IP's verbal prompts. The omission was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the fuel state during the working phase of the sortie, did not adjust the execution of the mission to the remaining flight time in the most efficient way, with the result of a minor deviation from the planned profile, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Orientation and the crosscheck of the A/C position against the Control and Performance Instruments were maintained throughout.

SP demonstrated airmanship within the desired standards, correlating the A/C state with the clearance received, performing all operational checks according to the Check List and the SOPs and carrying out the duties with minimum IP supervision. Task prioritization during the two consecutive approaches was accurate but reached the upper limit of the available capacity. Marginal performance for the Section - the margin of spare capacity under a compressed approach sequence is expected to improve.

SP demonstrated exceptional airmanship throughout the mission, identifying the contingencies of the deteriorating weather in advance and stating the divert criteria with their rationale before the descent. All operational checks were executed in the proper order according to the Check List, the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the SOPs, with negligible deviations, and the multitask sequence was handled without any item being dropped. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient study of the daily assignment, did not state the BOLD FACE steps of the simulated emergency in sequence and by heart, with the result that the IP had to prompt the critical actions and execute part of the procedure. The relevant Check List page was not identified without assistance. Further study of the emergency procedures and of the relevant systems is required.

SP applied the emergency procedure at the standard desired for this Training Section, completing the critical action steps and the follow-up items of the Check List after the IP's verbal prompts. Two steps were stated out of the standardized sequence and were corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Section - recall of the BOLD FACE steps by heart and without mistakes is expected to improve.

SP stated the BOLD FACE steps by heart and executed the follow-up items of the Check List without the IP's intervention, with minor errors in the order of two non-critical steps that were recognized and corrected in a timely manner. The A/C limits reported in Section V of the Flight Manual were observed throughout the handling. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP stated the proper steps of the critical action procedure in sequence, by heart and without mistakes, and executed the remaining actions according to the Check List and the IFG, without the IP's intervention, flawlessly and in a timely manner. The emergency was handled effectively while the instrument profile was maintained, and the A/C limits reported in Section V of the Flight Manual were observed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional knowledge of the emergency procedures and of the relevant systems, stating the BOLD FACE steps by heart, without mistakes and without hesitation, and completing the Check List and IFG items in the standardized sequence. The handling was integrated with the approach in progress: the controller was informed in plain language, the nearest suitable airfield was selected with its rationale and the A/C limits reported in Section V of the Flight Manual were observed with negligible deviations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to incomplete knowledge of the system affected by the simulated malfunction, did not execute the critical action steps in the standardized sequence and did not apply the corresponding Check List items, with the result that the IP directed the procedure and executed part of it. The A/C limits reported in Section V of the Flight Manual were not stated when requested. Further study of the emergency procedures set as daily assignment is required.

SP, due to a startle response that displaced the memorised recovery sequence, did not state the BOLD FACE steps in sequence and by heart at the onset of the simulated emergency, with the result that the critical actions were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts. The omitted step was recognized and corrected with delay, so the procedure was not executed in a timely manner.

SP handled the simulated emergency within the desired standards, stating the critical action steps by heart and completing the Check List items without the IP's intervention. The transition from the BOLD FACE steps to the follow-up items was made late on one occasion and was self-corrected. Marginal performance for the Section - speed of execution of the standardized sequence under instrument conditions is expected to improve.

SP stated the proper steps of the critical action procedure in sequence, by heart and without mistakes, and executed all remaining actions according to the Check List and the IFG without the IP's intervention, flawlessly and in a timely manner. The emergency was handled effectively, the A/C limits reported in Section V of the Flight Manual were observed and the approach was reconfigured accordingly. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional command of the emergency procedures and of the relevant systems, executing the BOLD FACE steps by heart, in sequence and without hesitation, while the instrument profile was maintained. The follow-up items of the Check List and the IFG were completed in the standardized sequence, the condition was passed to the controller in plain language and the recovery option was stated with its rationale. Knowledge of the A/C limits reported in Section V of the Flight Manual was exact, with negligible deviations in the handling. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition simulated, did not identify the emergency from the indications presented and did not state the corresponding critical action steps, with the result that the IP directed and executed the procedure. The A/C limits applicable to the condition were not known. Review of the emergency procedures and of the relevant systems set as daily assignment is required.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor system indication while the A/C state went unmonitored, did not proceed to the critical action steps of the applicable procedure and did not complete the corresponding Check List items, with the result that the sequence was executed only after the IP's verbal prompts. The correct procedure was identified and applied with delay, so the emergency was not handled in a timely manner.

SP, due to a non-standardized transition between the BOLD FACE steps and the Check List, executed two follow-up items out of the prescribed order during the simulated emergency, with the result of minor deviations from the standardized sequence, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. The critical action steps were stated by heart and the A/C limits reported in Section V of the Flight Manual were observed.

SP executed the emergency procedure within the desired standards, stating the critical action steps in sequence and by heart and completing the Check List and IFG items without the IP's intervention. Recall of the limits reported in Section V of the Flight Manual required prompting on one question during the post flight briefing. Marginal performance for the Section - depth of systems knowledge supporting the procedure is expected to improve.

SP demonstrated exceptional handling of the simulated emergency, stating every BOLD FACE step by heart, in sequence and without mistakes, and completing the Check List and IFG items flawlessly while flying the approach. The affected system, its reversion logic and the applicable limits reported in Section V of the Flight Manual were explained in detail at the post flight briefing, above the level expected for the Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient preparation of the daily assignment, did not state the minima and the required equipment for the planned instrument approach from the aeronautical publications, with the result that the IP provided the data and completed part of the flight planning. Questions on the Flight Manual limitations were not answered without assistance. Further study of the Flight Manual and of the aeronautical publications is required.

SP demonstrated general knowledge at the standard desired for this Training Section, locating the approach plate data and the holding speeds after the IP's verbal prompts. Answers on the AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 instrument requirements were given with delay and required correction. Marginal performance for the Section - detailed knowledge of the exercises set as daily assignment is expected to improve.

SP answered on the Flight Manual limitations and on the published approach criteria without the IP's support, with minor inaccuracies on the alternate airfield weather requirements that were recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Use of the aeronautical publications at the pre-flight briefing was confident. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knew in detail the exercises given as daily assignment and used the Flight Manual, the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the aeronautical publications with confidence at the pre-flight and post flight briefings. Meteorological principles, airport traffic procedures and the planning of the instrument mission were explained accurately and rapidly. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional theoretical knowledge for the level of the Training Section, explaining the approach criteria of the aeronautical publications, the corresponding AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 requirements and the Flight Manual limitations without any omission. The meteorological situation of the day was interpreted from the morning briefing and correlated with the selection of the alternate airfield, and the aerodynamic behavior expected during the penetration was explained theoretically. Knowledge of flight physiology and of the sea and land survival procedures was equally complete. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to incomplete study of the aeronautical publications, did not state the minima, the missed approach procedure and the navigation equipment required for the assigned approach, with the result that the IP provided the information and completed the mission planning. The relevant section of the Flight Manual was not located without assistance. Further study of the aeronautical publications and of the Flight Manual is required.

SP, due to insufficient knowledge of the system's reversion logic, did not explain the effect of the failure on the available navigation modes and did not relate it to the applicable Flight Manual limitations, with the result that the answer was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts. The incorrect explanation was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP demonstrated general knowledge within the desired standards, using the Flight Manual and the aeronautical publications with confidence and answering on the airport traffic procedures without the IP's support. Two answers on the meteorological minima for the alternate airfield were initially inaccurate and were self-corrected. Marginal performance for the Section - precision in the weather planning criteria is expected to improve.

SP knew in detail the exercises set as daily assignment and explained the provisions of the Flight Manual and of the Techniques and Procedures Manual applicable to the sortie accurately and rapidly. The AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 requirements, the meteorological principles and the airport traffic procedures were stated without the IP's support and were correctly applied to the flight plan. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional depth of general knowledge, explaining the instrument approach criteria of the aeronautical publications, the applicable AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 requirements and the corresponding Flight Manual limitations without any omission. The morning meteorological briefing was interpreted independently and translated into concrete divert criteria, and the aerodynamic effects expected during the penetration were explained theoretically. Knowledge of flight physiology and of the SAR rescue procedures was exact, with negligible gaps. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to lack of preparation of the material set as daily assignment, did not state the airport traffic procedures and the flight planning data required for the mission, with the result that the IP planned the profile and provided the publication references. The Flight Manual limitations applicable to the sortie were not known. Review of the Flight Manual, the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the aeronautical publications is required.

SP, due to lack of awareness of a published restriction that was available in the briefing material, did not apply the NOTAM in force affecting the assigned approach to the mission planning, with the result that the plan was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. The omission in the study of the aeronautical publications was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to an incomplete review of the meteorological part of the daily assignment, stated the alternate airfield weather requirements approximately and did not relate them to the forecast in force, with the result of minor inaccuracies in the planning, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Knowledge of the Flight Manual and of the airport traffic procedures was accurate throughout both briefings.

SP knew in detail the exercises set as daily assignment and used the Flight Manual, the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the aeronautical publications with confidence at both briefings. Answers on flight physiology and on the sea and land survival procedures were correct but were given slowly and after one prompt. Marginal performance for the Section - breadth of knowledge outside the daily assignment is expected to improve.

SP demonstrated exceptional general knowledge, explaining in detail the Flight Manual, the Techniques and Procedures Manual, the AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 provisions and the aeronautical publications applicable to the instrument mission. Meteorological principles, aerodynamics, airport traffic procedures, flight physiology and the sea and land survival and SAR rescue procedures were presented accurately and without prompting at the post flight briefing. Above end of block MIF achieved.
